title: fix(scripts): the polarity census reads a clause's prose, so a `never` annotation stops negating it (objectui#9832)
body:
Fixes #9832

## The defect

The polarity criterion is a regex that runs **on prose**, and it accepts `\bnever\b`.
A *declaring* clause can carry a **type annotation** that is also `never`:

> the TypeScript interface `S` declares `value?: never`

That sentence asserts that `S` **declares** `value` — a positive claim. The clause text
contains `never`, so polarity read **negative**, and the verdict inverted with it: under
the negative reading the entry "in contradiction" is the one that **has** the member,
exactly backwards.

`never` as a TypeScript type and `never` as an English adverb are indistinguishable to a
prose regex. That is a property of the instrument class — a criterion read over prose —
not a typo in one word list, and the triage comment asks for it to be treated as a
constraint on the fix rather than something to route around.

## Direction chosen: **A** (mask the backticked spans before reading polarity)

`segmentClauses` now hands each clause **both readings of itself** and they are not
interchangeable: `text` is the clause as written (what a report shows a human), `prose`
is the clause with its backticked spans still masked (the only text a word-level
criterion may be read over). `readPolarity` reads the negators, and the leading-negator
test, over `prose`. The mask keeps a **placeholder** rather than deleting the span,
because an offset has to survive for a key to stay locatable in the clause it was
written in.

### Why not B (exclude `never` only at the annotation position)

⭐ **Measured, and it decided this**: the corpus carries a second spelling of the same
inversion that an annotation-position rule does not reach. In
`.changeset/6355-retire-timeline-timescale-alias.md` the negating `never` is a **call
expression**, the zod twin of a tombstone:

> the Zod twin declares `z.never().optional()`

A key in the following clause inherits that declaration clause, so the inversion travels
with it. B repairs the annotation instance and leaves this one. A repairs both, and the
pin `covers the CALL EXPRESSION, not just the annotation` is that leg.

### Why not C (accept it as the Nth POLARITY residue and document it)

C is a legitimate outcome and the card says so. It is refused here on evidence, not
taste: this spelling is ADR-0049's by-name refusal tombstone (settled on objectui#9764),
so the misreading is **growing with the corpus** rather than sitting still — every future
changeset describing a tombstone would read inverted. A costs three behavioural lines and
is provably invariant on the pinned blind spot (below), so the residue C would have
documented is not worth keeping. The header's limitation list is edited either way, and
it is edited here: the POLARITY entry now records this repair and names what it did NOT
move.

### The four axes

- **实际业务需求** — the inversion is live, not speculative: it is reproduced at this
  branch's merge base on three real pending changesets (delta below), and the spelling
  that triggers it is the one this lane just standardised. The instrument's readers are
  the seats adjudicating changeset claims.
- **项目长远合理性** — positional, not lexical. The repair says *a word inside a code span
  is not a word of the sentence*, which is the general statement; a word-list carve-out
  would have been a patch on one token and the next code word would re-open it.
- **防 AI 写代码犯错** — an inverted verdict on a tombstone sentence is the worst shape for
  this instrument: it tells a reader that the schema **declaring** the tombstone is the
  one in contradiction, which points a repair at correct prose. Two such repairs were
  explicitly refused on this card.
- **创业阶段不扩散需求** — nothing published moves, no capability is added, no accepted
  input set is relaxed. The changeset carries empty frontmatter, which is this repo's
  explicit "no release" declaration.

## ⛔ Two fences, both honoured

1. **`never` was NOT deleted from the negator list.** It is a real English negator, and a
   sentence reading "the renderer never reads it" must keep reading negative. The DARK LEG
   pin asserts it, and asserts the same word in **both positions of one sentence** reading
   both ways at once.
2. **No changeset body was repaired.** `.changeset/6951-text-value-retired.md` and
   `.changeset/6951-tree-view-data-retired.md` are untouched — the diff is four files and
   neither is among them.

## Evidence

Merge base: `4d963a26b1626e7e91dcea450ecc5a80adaf78f4` (computed here; the dispatch quoted
`3ae740c4a8` as a tip, and nothing has touched this file between the two —
`git log 3ae740c4a8..HEAD -- scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` is empty).

**Premise reproduces.** Both `6951-*` entries read `polarity: negative` with
`memberPresent: true` at the merge base, on the sentence that asserts the interface
declares the tombstone. Confirmed before any edit.

### Full delta, key by key — ⛔ not a net count

Taken over the whole matched population (303 rows, both corpora dumped before and after
from `census()`'s own `matched`, so a flag that APPEARS is visible as well as one that
vanishes). Exactly **six rows moved**, every one of them `negative` to `positive`:

| entry | schema.key | polarity | member | flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `6951-text-value-retired.md` | `TextSchema.value` | neg to pos | present | flag to no flag |
| `6951-tree-view-data-retired.md` | `TreeViewSchema.data` | neg to pos | present | flag to no flag |
| `6355-retire-timeline-timescale-alias.md` | `TimelineSchema.timeScale` | neg to pos | present | flag to no flag |
| `6951-text-value-retired.md` | `BaseSchema.value` | neg to pos | absent | no flag to flag |
| `6355-retire-timeline-timescale-alias.md` | `TimelineSchema.invalid_type` | neg to pos | absent | no flag to flag |
| `6355-retire-timeline-timescale-alias.md` | `TimelineSchema.expected` | neg to pos | absent | no flag to flag |

⭐ **`6355-retire-timeline-timescale-alias.md` is a THIRD instance of this defect that the
card does not name** — it reads "`TimelineSchema.timeScale` is declared `?: never`", a
positive assertion about a member that is present, and it was flagged. It is repaired by
the same change. Reported rather than absorbed, per the dispatch.

⭐ **The three rows that gained a flag are not a trade, and none of them is a lost
detection.** Each is a row whose polarity is now **right** and whose flag comes from a
limit this instrument's header already names: `BaseSchema.value` is WINDOW PAIRING (the
sentence names two schemas and V pairs the key with both), and `invalid_type` / `expected`
are the KEY EXTRACTION residue (a zod error code is spelled exactly like a member key).
Both were previously **silenced by the inverted polarity** — a wrong reading producing an
accidentally quiet answer. The census is report-only and a flag is a CANDIDATE, so
un-silencing them is the honest outcome; ⛔ neither belongs to this card to narrow.

**The bounded transition this change made**: I moved three rows from a negative reading to
a positive one and out of contradiction, and three rows inherited the corrected polarity
and became candidates. ⛔ Not a claim about what the census reports on any later tree.

### The objectui#9727 blind-spot fixture: I did not change its verdicts

`diff` of the full fixture population before and after is **byte-identical** — all 24 rows,
not only the flagged ones. The four pinned keys (`allowCollapse`, `cardTitle`, `columns`,
`titleField`) are all still `negative`, all still `viaPronoun`, all still flagged.

⚠️ **A correction to the card, measured rather than assumed.** The card and the claim
comment both state that one of those four is judged negative via a prose `never`. It is
not. Their negator is the prose `none` of *"The surviving `ObjectKanbanSchema` face
declares none of them"*, and the word `never` **does not occur anywhere in the fixture
corpus** — `grep -roF never` reads 0 with `exit=1` (defaulted explicitly), against lit
controls in the same corpus and the same instrument: `none` reads 3, `not` reads 10, and
the corpus carries 50 backticked spans of which **zero** contain a negator word. ⇒ the
masking is structurally incapable of reaching that fixture, which is stronger than the
verdicts merely happening to match. What makes the **word list** safe is the DARK LEG pin,
not the fixture — and that is now said in the pin's own comment so the next reader does
not inherit the wrong reason.

### Ablation — the pin goes red without the fix

Mutation leg took `scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` back to the merge-base version
and proved on disk it landed before reading any result:

```
--- PRE-MUTATION on-disk markers ---
fixed-marker  'NEGATIVE.test(c.prose)' exit=0 count=1
defect-marker 'NEGATIVE.test(c.text)'  exit=1 count=0
--- POST-MUTATION on-disk markers ---
fixed-marker  exit=1 count=0
defect-marker exit=0 count=1
disk blob now = 595cb1a5a6ac3b43d76683a0f531221e38e4db2c  (HEAD blob = 5e048b85efd6f43e9af22fee97a3a36a901cd220)
--- RUN the new pin against the mutated instrument ---
ABLATION vitest exit=1
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  5 failed | 44 passed (49)
```

The five that go red are every new pin **except** `⛔ did NOT buy it with blindness` — that
one is the invariance leg and is green on both sides **by design**, which is what an
invariance assertion means. Stated rather than left to look like a weak pin.

Restore leg is symmetric and was verified by state, not by an exit code:
`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` (spelled with a placeholder word, never with an angle-bracket shape, because this body's sanitizer eats those; never a bare checkout — a bare one restores from the
polluted index), post-restore `git hash-object` equals the HEAD blob
`5e048b85efd6f43e9af22fee97a3a36a901cd220`, markers reversed, and `git diff HEAD --stat` is
empty. The script carried `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths throughout.

### Gates

Run at this branch's head, targeted per the repo's own instruction that whole-farm
enumeration belongs to CI:

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/changeset-polarity-census.test.ts` — **49 passed**
  (43 before; the 6 new pins are this card's). Run through the shared verify lock.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` — **173 passed, 2 skipped (175 files); 5117 tests passed**.
  The whole `scripts/` suite, because the edited module is shared; its only in-tree readers
  are its own test, its fixtures and `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:changeset-claims` ·
  `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:comment-mask-corpus`
  · `check:doc-fences` — all **exit 0**, each captured to a file before any pipe.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0, prints *"No source or published
  contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."* An
  empty-frontmatter changeset is added anyway, which is this repo's explicit "not
  released" declaration.
- `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` — exit 0; the new fixture is already
  covered by the ledger's `corpus/**` entry, so CI's markdown stage still runs the shards
  for it (verified with `--changed`).
- `pnpm exec eslint` on both edited sources — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 files linted (count
  read from `--format json`, not from a silent exit).
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` — **NOT GOVERNED**, 4 paths checked
  against 5 governed surfaces, none matched. Ordinary review and merge-queue route.

## Acceptance notes

- **Serial fence respected.** Nothing here touches objectui#9767's subject (the "schema not
  in corpus" vs "schema gone" conflation) even though it lives in this file, and nothing
  touches the objectui#9754 slice-2 subject. Both sit after this card on the fence, and
  both will sample an output this card has moved — the delta table above is what they
  sample from.
- **Residue named, not hidden.** Only the polarity read moved to `prose`. The population
  predicate (`PRESENT_DECLARATION`) still reads the restored clause, so a declaration verb
  written inside a backticked span still opens a declaration clause. That is a population
  question, not a polarity one; it is written into the header's limits list rather than
  fixed here.
- *noted, not filed*: the `invalid_type` / `expected` rows in
  `6355-retire-timeline-timescale-alias.md` are a live instance of the header's own KEY
  EXTRACTION residue — a zod error code spelled exactly like a member key. Not a new
  defect and not in the three fileable classes; it is already named in the instrument's
  own limits list. Successor: whoever takes the WINDOW PAIRING question, since the header
  routes it there.
- Session, as prose so it survives a body rewrite: `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`.
